transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m convinced some labs are secretly using people like my mom and our community in dangerous experiments, and no one can show me anything that truly proves otherwise. That is the main reason I am here today, because everyone else just dismisses what is happening.
How has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling very down and depressed, or on the contrary, unusually energetic and on top of the world?
My mood has been relatively normal, and I haven't felt particularly depressed or unusually energetic. I'm just really stressed and anxious about these experiments and trying to keep my mom safe.
Have you ever heard voices talking when no one else was around, or seen things that other people couldn't see?

No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that weren't actually there. My senses are completely clear, and I am only reacting to the very real patterns and lab orders that I see with my own eyes at work.
Apart from your worries about these experiments, have you noticed any changes in your motivation, your ability to work, or your interest in your usual hobbies?

My ability to work is still mostly fine, and I keep up with my daily shifts drawing blood, though my supervisors just think I'm a bit too intense. But my relationships with my family are really strained because I keep pushing them to change my mom's doctors, and I've been avoiding certain coworkers I suspect are involved.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were not your own—such as being put into your mind or taken out by an outside force—or that others could somehow hear or read your thoughts?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. My thoughts are entirely my own, and I've never felt like anyone was putting ideas into my head, taking them out, or reading my mind.
How long have you been noticing these patterns and suspecting that these secret lab experiments are taking place?
I've been noticing these patterns for about a year now. It started right around the time my mom's diabetes complications got worse and I began accompanying her to all of her specialist appointments.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with non-bizarre delusions (believing secret labs are performing dangerous experiments on her mother and community) lasting for approximately one year. Her daily functioning and work performance are relatively preserved, which is characteristic of Delusional Disorder. Schizophrenia (F20.9) was ruled out due to the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or thought alienation. Mood disorders with psychotic features were also ruled out as she reports a normal mood without manic or major depressive episodes.
